title: Future
author: andyisalreadydead
selftext:
Hey! I'm 33M. I started to learn how to make games 2 years ago, but I'm still very novice. This is just a hobby for me and I had several ones, but lately gamedev became my only one. I also plan to use my own art, so I need to learn how to draw. 

I have some ideas in my head, but they are mostly complex projects, so I need to dramatically increase my skill. It's gonna take some years, probably more than 5 years. Probably close to 10. And today I ponder if it even makes sense. I believe the world will be very different in 10 years due to AI. I'm afraid I'm gonna invest time in skills that will be absolutely obsolete in that time frame. But just wait and see isn't seems like an option either. I need something to do to escape from pretty sad life I have nowadays and I want it to be beneficial and useful in future. I don't do things only for process, I need to grow some potential. 

Could you please share you thoughts about this situation. Maybe you’ve been through it too.

comments.author: Big_Whale_95
comments.body:
That's a hard one. Just get started. Prototype. 

I guess game and system design, and the understanding how it works and how it should play is always important. 

If you develop with ai, try to nail systems and user experience and not graphics. 

Some of the most detail and complex games are years old and look outdated but charming. 

Most important: hust have fun while doing it. And see it from the eyes of a player .

Hope that helped

comments.author: AbsentAgent
comments.body: Hey I've been trying to develop games for 6+ years and have never shipped a title as an indie dev, however even with the drastically changing landscape due to A.I I'm an advocate for keeping up with a "super intelligence explosion" and that comes with cross training and skills, so spend less time pondering and more time doing, because all the programming, 3D modeling, proc-gen, animation, writing, level design, sound design and music making, drawing, design, color theory are all skills that enable learning and lessons in other fields. No skill spent in earnest practice should feel like a waste, complex ideas take time, and that doesn't mean they're good ideas, so start small start simple and get making. Make smaller games with components of your complex idea and get feedback from players, try a game jam or two with collaborators and make connections.

comments.author: General_Correct
comments.body: Ai will solve the coding, art and music part pretty fast. You just need to adapt and learn fast enough to understand what is good and what is not. Game design, level design, replayability, fun, as well new gimmicks, new mechanics and unexpected plot twists and gameplay twists right now seem to be hard to be generated by AI, so it will stay in human hands for longer, but i think it’s solvable too, as soon as a proper automated market research for games and what people like will appear

replies.author: AceHighness
replies.body: my automated game studio uses several internet feeds to generate game trend information (like which game types are currently hot), that is later used by an agent who generates pitches for new game titles. this is very basic and not what you are talking about, but its a step in that direction. will have to ponder about what you said and how that can be made reality.

comments.author: pimpelimpe3
comments.body:
A warm recommendation from my heart.  
Figure out what game you can complete with the skills you have right now . However tiny or insignificant it might feel compared to your bigger dreams and plans.   
No skill will ever serve you better than learning to take any idea and actually complete it. It does not have to be good. It does not have to be original. It just not need to be your art.   
Just wrap One game.

And then another 😉 and your skills will explode because you will learn only what you really need to do the next game 

I wish you the best -

comments.author: RoboProletariat
comments.body: Just get started. It's not like AI solves everything. You just get to learn Game Dev AND AI Tool Management now.

comments.author: jocktor
comments.body: AI will free you up to do the things you want. Not take them away.

comments.author: EntropyMonkey
comments.body: I am in a similar situation. I also started with game dev a little more than 2 years ago, and I am currently asking myself strongly whether it is even still worth learning all the skills that might become obsolete in a short time. I have made the decision for myself to continue investing in these skills. Even if they are no longer needed one day, you will still keep the experience. This experience can make the difference in the future between a game dev who can only operate AI and a game dev who also possesses a deeper understanding of the underlying things. I believe that this will always be an advantage, but only a few will learn these skills to this depth in the future, because it will simply be too strenuous and time-consuming, and that will be an advantage for you. Knowledge is power. That is why I continue to invest time and work on my first indie game without AI, so that I have created at least one game completely without AI. After that, I can use AI and hopefully become a better game dev through it.

comments.author: Decent_Departure9874
comments.body: Yes, AI is going to change things a lot! Especially hard skills like coding... still relevant to learn, but i think the main skill you want to develop is using AI to build games. That is a skill that will be needed in the future more and more. So, focus on working with agents and be effective in that way. This should set you up nicely dor the future, while making games
